thread.title: Be afraid? Investors are eating up stocks at the fastest pace in years

author: morningstar.com
title: Be afraid? Investors are eating up stocks at the fastest pace in years
text:
By Shawn Langlois, MarketWatch
Critical information for the U.S. trading day
The "very stable genius" (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/president-trump-says-he-is-fit-for-office-and-proclaims-he-is-a-very-stable-genius-2018-01-06) calling the shots in the White House loves dangling the freight-training stock market in front of America as an affirmation of his bigly productive first year. And investors, if the latest reading from the AAII survey is any indication, are betting the "enormously consensual" (http://thehill.com/homenews/administration/367860-trump-misQuote: s-ny-post-column-touts-his-consensual-presidency) president will keep driving those record gains.
Or at least not get in the way.
As you can see from our chart of the day,via Dana Lyons of J. Lyons Fund Management (http://jlfmi.tumblr.com/post/169353075190/stock-allocations-approaching-dotcom-levels), individual investors haven't been this heavy into equities since back in 2000, during the fragile peak of the dot-com bubble.
The December reading shows stock allocation jumped from 69% to 72%, which trails the 77% level reached before the epic implosion nearly two decades ago. The 3-percentage-point jump is the biggest monthly increase in four years. Does that mean a collapse is imminent?
Of course not. Maybe.
"In the near-term, the stock market will do whatever it wants," Lyons writes. "That includes the possibility of rallying for several more years, despite the present elevated reading."
He notes that stocks managed to rally for years following the 72% reading registered in 1997. Lyons, however, isn't exactly feeling bullish about a repeat of that.
"This reading implies a significant level of potential longer-term risk," he says. "If the market does start to head meaningfully lower, this condition could exacerbate the decline, given the amount of capital with the potential to exit the market. In such an event, the substantial potential risk could, thus, become manifested risk."
Read more:Bullish sentiment for U.S. stocks is at a seven-year high (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/bullish-sentiment-for-us-stocks-is-at-a-seven-year-high-2018-01-05)
Key market gauges
Futures for the Dow and the S&P are little changed, while Europe (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stocks-stick-to-2-year-highs-despite-german-orders-disappointment-2018-01-08) is up a bit. Asian equities (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-largely-gain-though-regulatory-moves-weigh-in-china-hong-kong-2018-01-07) were mostly high ahead of the region's earnings season this week.
Bitcoin (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/bitcoin-pulls-back-further-from-17000-2018-01-08) is down back below $16,000. Gold is leaning a bit lower, while crude is higher.
Read the Market Snapshot (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dow-poised-to-stretch-out-historic-record-run-as-upbeat-mood-persists-2018-01-08) for more.
The buzz
Shh! Elon Musk's SpaceX successfully launched a Falcon 9 rocket (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/spacex-successfully-launches-secret-satellite-after-weeks-long-delay-2018-01-07) carrying a secret government payload into orbit on Sunday night from Cape Canaveral. Not much in the way of details about the classified mission have emerged, other than that it includes a satellite built by Northrop Grumman (NOC) .
Activist shareholders want Apple (AAPL) to help kids kick their iPhone addictions (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/activist-shareholders-want-apple-to-help-kids-kick-iphone-addictions-2018-01-07).
Chip maker Nvidia has landed Uber as a self-driving tech partner (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/nvidia-lands-uber-as-self-driving-partner-to-kick-off-ces-2018-01-08) to kick off the CES conference.
Celgene (CELG) says it will buy blood-disease specialist Impact Biomedicines (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/celgene-said-to-be-near-7-billion-deal-to-buy-impact-biomedicines-2018-01-07) for as much as $7 billion.
See:Why 2018 is a make-or-break year for pharma (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/why-2018-is-a-make-or-break-year-for-pharma-2017-12-19)
Pfizer (PFE) said Saturday it's done trying to discover new drugs for Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson's disease. Too costly and, to this point, too futile. The cutback will cost 300 jobs (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/pfizer-abandons-costly-hunt-for-new-alzheimers-parkinsons-drugs-2018-01-07) in Cambridge and Andover in Massachusetts and in Groton, Conn.
The call
General Electric (GE) was the dog of the Dow in 2017, losing almost half its value during the broad market rally. Well, 2018 is a completely different story so far, with GE and its 6% surge beating all other blue chips.
Of course, it's only been a few days, but that's enough to trigger a potential breakout, according to The Street's Jonas Elmerraji (https://www.thestreet.com/story/14437855/1/general-electric-could-break-higher-within-days-as-dow-soars.html?puc=yahoo&cm_ven=YAHOO&yptr=yahoo), who uses this chart to paint a bullish picture for the coming months.
"After lagging the rest of the Dow in a big way for the last year, this is a mean-reversion trade," Elmerraji writes. "Now, just to be clear, higher ground for the last four or five sessions alone isn't a signal that GE's last year of selling is over. Instead, that turnaround is being signaled by where those recent sessions have left shares."
Specifically, he says GE is now trading around its 50-day moving average, and a move above that means a change in trend that could deliver the goods.
"This could be the start of a big, sustained move in this industrial sector giant," he says.
Check out:2018's best-performing blue chips support the Dogs of the Dow theory (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/2018s-best-performing-blue-chips-support-the-dogs-of-the-dow-theory-2018-01-05)

There are just so, SO many morsels from this epic Stephen Miller interview (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trump-aide-stephen-miller-cut-off-during-contentious-cnn-interview-2018-01-07) with Jake Tapper on CNN.

The stat
$830 billion -- That's the market capitalization of the total cryptocurrency universe, which broke through the $800-billion level for the first time over the weekend. That's even as bitcoin, by far the biggest player, trades well below its record peak (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/bitcoin-pulls-back-further-from-17000-2018-01-08).
The economy
The key figures to watch this week don't really hit until Friday, when we get December retail sales. The end of week will also unofficially kick off fourth-quarter earnings season, with J.P. Morgan Chase (JPM), Wells Fargo (WFC) and BlackRock (BLK) all scheduled to report.
As for today's sparse schedule, the Fed releases its consumer credit reading at 3:00 p.m. Eastern.
